urocortin injected into the lateral septal intermediate region decreases food intake without producing a conditioned taste aversion and blocks orexin-induced feeding.
UCN in the lateral septum inhibits feeding induced both by deprivation and by orexin A injection into the lateral hypothalamic area.
urocortin in lateral septum (1) significantly inhibits feeding in food-depivied rats and (2) significantly decreases orexin A-induced food intake in the lateral hypothalamic area.

the neuroanatomical organization of the hypothalamus and the role of corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH)-related peptides and receptors in regulating feeding behavior.

how stress and anxiety affect feeding and how the hypothalamus regulates food intake.

UCN in the lateral septum modulates feeding induced via orexin A in lateral hypothalamus, and this effect is mediated by CRH receptor 2.

UCN in the LS is anorectic and this effect is mediated by CRH receptors.
